                    ### Question
                    A 72-year-old male visits his gastroenterologist for a check-up one year following resection of a 2-cm malignant lesion in his sigmoid colon. Serum levels of which of the following can be used in this patient to test for cancer recurrence?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Alpha-fetoprotein
opb. Carcinoembryonic antigen
opc. Cancer antigen 125 (CA-125)
opd. Gamma glutamyl transferase
ope. CA-19-9 tumor marker

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Monitoring carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) levels is commonly used for colorectal cancer recurrence detection. Gamma glutamyl transferase (GGT) and CA-125 are not typically used for this purpose. CA-19-9 tumor marker is associated with pancreatic cancer, not colorectal cancer recurrence.
